chunks: From Hakimah, like the meaning of the first hadith, except that she said: 'Abu Muhammad (peace be upon him) sent for me on the night of the fifteenth of Ramadan, the year two hundred and fifty-five…' I said to him, 'O son of Allah's Messenger, who is his mother?' He said: 'Narjis.' She said: 'When it was the third day, my longing for the Wali of Allah intensified, so I went to visit them. I began with the room where the slave girl was, and there I found her sitting in the manner of a postpartum woman, wearing yellow clothes, with her head wrapped. I greeted her and looked to the side of the room, and there was a cradle covered with green sheets. I turned to the cradle and lifted the sheets, and there I was with the Wali of Allah sleeping on his back, neither fastened nor swaddled. He opened his eyes and began laughing and calling me with his finger. I took him and brought him near my mouth to kiss him, and I smelled from him a fragrance that I had never smelled anything sweeter than. Abu Muhammad (peace be upon him) called out to me: 'O my aunt! Come, bring my young man to me.' I took him and he said: 'O my son, speak…' And he narrated the hadith.'
ai.seo_question: Who is the mother of Imam Hasan al-Askari and when was he born?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Kitab al-Ghayba* provides a detailed eyewitness account of the birth of Imam al-Mahdi (peace be upon him) on the 15th of Ramadan, 255 AH, to Imam Hasan al-Askari and his mother Narjis. It highlights the miraculous nature of his birth, including his immediate alertness and the fragrant scent reported by the narrator, serving as a key evidence for the Shia belief in his hidden existence and divine designation.
